title: The Missing Master

opening.text: LP? It's Marisol, housekeeping, floor fourteen. I can't find my master card. Or the closet key. They were on my trolley. I've looked everywhere. I'm so sorry.

briefing: 23:20. A room attendant reports that her floor master keycard (floors 12 to 14) and the mechanical key to those floors' service closets are missing from her trolley.

Veldane key control: a lost master is disabled the moment it is reported, then investigated. A master card opens every guest room on three floors. As supervisor, you also decide what the mechanical key costs to fix, within your authority of 2,500.
learningObjectives: Disable first: a lost master is voided at once
Lock audit and CCTV: was the key used after it went missing?
Proportionate re-keying, and coaching staff without blame

actions.label: Void the master card in the lock system
actions.finding: Card HK-M12-14-03 voided at {time}; every lock on floors 12 to 14 will refuse it from its next use. A new master is encoded and held at the desk for the housekeeping supervisor.

actions.label: Pull the lock audit for card HK-M12-14-03
finding: The card opened 1411 at 22:31 (Marisol's last room). At 22:52 it opened 1415, which is vacant and ready. At 22:54 it was used at 1417 and refused: the guest's deadbolt was on.
Nothing after 22:54. Marisol says she noticed it missing at about 23:10.

actions.label: Talk to Marisol
actions.finding: She clipped the card and the closet key to the top tray of her trolley while she turned down 1411, "because the coil hurts my wrist". The trolley was outside the door for about eight minutes. She noticed at 23:10, searched, then called. She is frightened of losing her job.

lines.speaker: attendant_duarte
lines.text: I put them on the tray, just for that room. The coil hurts my wrist. I know I shouldn't. Am I going to lose my job?

actions.label: Search the trolley and the closet with Marisol
actions.finding: With her there and her agreement: not on the trolley, in the linen, or in the closet. The tray clip is empty.

actions.label: Check 1415 and the door of 1417 with Ines
actions.finding: 1415: vacant, made up, nothing disturbed, minibar sealed. 1417: you do not knock; the door is locked, the deadbolt indicator shows engaged, no sound of distress. You leave a note for the morning to speak to the guest with the duty manager.

actions.label: Review the floor 14 corridor camera
finding: 22:33 the trolley stands outside 1411 with nobody near it. 22:38 a man in a grey cap and dark jacket walks from the lifts, lifts something from the top tray without breaking stride and goes to the far end.
22:52 he enters 1415 and comes out at 22:53 with nothing in his hands. 22:54 he tries 1417, waits, and leaves by Stair A at 22:55. His face is never clear; the cap hides it.
rows: Man in grey cap takes something from the top tray

actions.label: Check the key log in housekeeping
actions.finding: HK-M12-14-03 and closet key K-SC-12-14 signed out at 15:00 by M. Duarte, not returned. Every other master is signed back. The log shows two "lost card" entries this year, both found again the same night.

actions.label: Report the theft to the police
actions.finding: DS Ruth Calloway takes the report: theft of a master card, entry to a vacant room, attempted entry to an occupied one. She asks you to preserve the floor 14 and lift footage and the lock audit, and gives a reference.

lines.speaker: police_liaison
lines.text: Thanks for calling it in tonight, not next week. Keep the footage and the lock report for me. I'll be in tomorrow.

actions.label: Brief the night manager
actions.finding: Felix Amadi agrees to speak to the guest in 1417 with you after 08:00, and to tell the executive housekeeper first thing.

actions.label: Talk to Marisol about what happens now
actions.finding: You tell her what the camera shows, that reporting it quickly limited the damage, and that keys stay on the person, always; you will ask housekeeping for a softer wrist coil. She signs a short statement.

questions.prompt: Marisol asks if she is going to lose her job. What do you say?

options.label: "That isn't my decision, and I won't pretend. What I can tell you is that calling straight away was exactly right. Let's find out what happened."
options.feedback: Honest, calm, and you reward the report. Staff who fear blame hide lost keys; that is when they get used.

reply.speaker: attendant_duarte
reply.text: Okay. Okay. Thank you. What do you need from me?

options.label: "No, of course not. Don't worry about it."
options.feedback: Kind, but not yours to promise, and it may not be true.

options.label: "Losing a master is a serious breach. You know the policy."
options.feedback: True, and the fastest way to make sure the next lost key is not reported.

questions.prompt: The closet key K-SC-12-14 is still out there. What do you do about it?

options.label: Have engineering re-core the three closet locks on floors 12 to 14 tonight from the spare cores: about 540.
options.feedback: Proportionate: the key opens three closets with chemicals and linen; the fix is cheap, quick and within your authority.

options.label: Re-key the whole back-of-house master system: about 48,000.
options.feedback: Far above your authority and out of proportion: the lost key is not a system master. Escalating a plan like this would be the right form; spending it is not.

options.label: Nothing. It's only a closet key.
options.feedback: Those closets hold chemicals and master linen, and someone who stole a master card took this key with it.

questions.prompt: Someone tried 1417 in the night. What does the guest hear, and when?

options.label: In the morning, from the duty manager with you: what happened, that the card is voided and the police informed, and what the hotel will do. Don't wake her tonight: her door held and the card is dead.
options.feedback: She has a right to know, in person, with facts and a plan; waking her at midnight adds fear and no safety.

options.label: Nothing. Nobody got in.
options.feedback: Someone tried her door with a stolen master card. She will hear it from the police if not from you.

options.label: Knock now and tell her.
options.feedback: Well meant, but the danger has passed and the card is voided. Frightening her at midnight helps nobody.

options.label: A floor master card and closet key were taken from an unattended trolley on 14 at 22:38; the card opened vacant 1415 and was refused at 1417; voided at {time:void_card}; police informed.
options.feedback: The key facts in order, including the attempted entry.

options.label: Room attendant lost her master key.
options.feedback: The camera shows it was taken. "Lost" also puts the blame on her and hides the attempted entry.

options.label: Master key stolen due to staff carelessness.
options.feedback: A judgement, not a fact. Report what happened; the cause analysis comes later.

questions.prompt: Incident report, which of these belong in the findings?

options.label: 14-02: a man in a grey cap takes an item from the trolley tray at 22:38 and leaves by Stair A at 22:55.
Key log: both items signed out to M. Duarte at 15:00, not returned.
Card voided at {time:void_card}; closet locks re-cored; police reference obtained.
It was probably an inside job.
options.feedback: Nothing you have shows that. Speculation in a report can damage people who did nothing.

checks.label: Disable at once
checks.pass: The master was dead within minutes of the report.
checks.fail: A working master card for three floors stayed live while you investigated.

checks.label: Void before searching
checks.pass: Disable first, then look for it. If it turns up, a new card costs nothing.
checks.fail: You searched for the card while it still worked.

checks.label: Was it used?
checks.pass: The lock audit turned a lost key into a theft with an attempted entry.
checks.fail: You never asked the locks whether the card was used.

checks.label: Who took it?
checks.pass: The corridor camera shows how it went, and that Marisol did not lose it.
checks.fail: Without the footage, it stays her fault and nobody looks for the man in the cap.

checks.label: Check the rooms it touched
checks.pass: 1415 checked, 1417 confirmed secure without waking the guest.
checks.fail: You never checked the rooms the card was used on.

checks.label: Report the crime
checks.pass: Theft of a master card and an attempted entry are crimes; the police have them tonight.

checks.label: Coach, don't blame
checks.pass: She knows what happened, why keys stay on the person, and that reporting fast was right.
checks.fail: Marisol went home thinking she was about to be fired, and learned nothing.

debrief.whatHappened: A man walked past an unattended trolley, took the master card from the tray, let himself into a vacant room and tried an occupied one. The deadbolt in 1417 stopped him; your void stopped the card. The lock audit and the camera turned "lost key" into what it was.
bestPractice: Void a lost electronic master the moment it is reported; investigate after.
Pull the lock audit: every door the card touched since it went missing.
Check the rooms involved; decide with the duty manager how and when to tell affected guests.
Review CCTV on the floor and the routes off it.
Check the key log: who signed it out, when, and what else is missing.
Fix mechanical keys in proportion to what they open: re-core the few locks a lost key fits.
Report a theft or attempted entry to the police and preserve the evidence.
Coach the employee: keys stay on the person; quick reporting is thanked, not punished.
debrief.why: A master card is a key to every guest on the floor. The minutes between loss and void are the dangerous ones, and staff only report quickly if reporting is safe for them.
commonMistakes: Searching for an hour before voiding.
Calling it "lost" without checking the locks.
Waking guests at midnight to tell them.
Blaming the attendant so the next loss goes unreported.

lesson: Void first, then ask the locks, the cameras and the log what happened.
